subject.title: [Feature Request]: Multi-lane concurrency support for sub-agents via sessions_spawn

question: Should subagent isolation extend the existing derived-lane model, use target-agent configuration, or expose caller-selected lane names through `sessions_spawn`?
rationale: The feature gap is confirmed, but the owner of scheduling policy determines the model-facing tool contract, configuration shape, observability, resource safety, and compatibility behavior.

options.title: Extend derived lanes
options.body: Derive bounded subagent lanes from stable task, target-agent, or parent-session identity while retaining a global resource cap.

options.title: Expose spawn lanes
options.body: Add a validated caller-selected lane and per-lane configuration while preserving the current default.

options.title: Use agent-owned limits
options.body: Keep the spawn tool unchanged and isolate work exclusively through target-agent concurrency policy.

recommendation.title: Extend derived lanes
recommendation.body: Derive bounded subagent lanes from stable task, target-agent, or parent-session identity while retaining a global resource cap.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest feature-history and discussion connection to the original spawn and concurrency contracts.
